transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29 11:00 PT / 18:00 UTC
Duration: ~37 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Lena (Aether VP Product), Marcus (Aether Staff Eng), Raj (Aether Security), Priya (Aether PM)

Summary: quick postmortem on SDK function-callback failures seen during pilot, review of latency/throughput numbers, discuss fallback behavior (hosted -> dedicated fallthrough), action items for reproducing and hardening SDK, next steps for security review and pricing.

Topics: SDK callback timeout, structured output parsing mismatches, KV cache warming, batching config, graceful fallback to smaller model, VPC/KMS questions, benchmark plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: alright good morning everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda — we want to walk through the callback failures you saw yesterday, share the tracing we pulled, and agree on repro steps and next actions. Omar's got the sandbox traces ready.
[00:18] Omar: hey team, yeah i've got the traces. quick note — i'm going to read some raw snippets so there might be noise; please interrupt. the failure mode we saw looked like: request hits Redwood hosted tier, we return a 202 for streaming start, but the SDK on the customer side raised a callback timeout at ~6s and then retried, which sometimes resulted in duplicate function invocations.
[00:37] Marcus: yeah that's what we observed — the client SDK retries after a 5 to 6s ack window and then we get two function calls which breaks idempotency in our downstream. we instrumented with a local trace and saw the initial llama-ish generation step still running on the server for another 2–3s after the client gave up.
[01:04] Priya: to add context, our success criteria for the pilot include no duplicate invocations across 95% of calls, and median latency < 350ms for synchronous paths. this callback behavior is the blocker.
[01:20] Omar: understoood. couple of clarifications — are you on the latest SDK? there was a patch last week that changed retry backoff behavior for streaming ACKs.
[01:31] Marcus: we are on 0.9.2, i think the patch is in 0.9.3 but we didn't pick it up because we pinned versions in the pipeline. i'll share the exact lockfile.
[01:42] Lena: also called out — some outputs are structured JSON arrays and when we get dups, our ingestion pipeline dedupe fails because the request id isn't consistent. it's a mix of SDK-side id generation and server-supplied ids.
[02:01] Omar: ok that helps. from Redwood's traces we see two things: first, there's a slow prefix cache miss on certain long prompt contexts — kv cache warming added ~120ms in a few samples; second, we see the streaming ACK not reaching the client before they hit their local timeout threshold in a few spots.
[02:27] Maya: the important piece here is the interplay: client timeout + SDK retries + server-side batching and cache warmups. we need short term mitigation and longer term fixes.
[02:38] Raj: from security side, while we're on the call — when there's dedupe or retries, we worry about data-leakage into logs and duplicate writes to audit trails. if callbacks are retried we need idempotency tokens to be passed through and logged with correlation ids.
[02:58] Omar: agreed. recommended immediate mitigation we can push: 1) upgrade SDK to 0.9.3 (fixes aggressive retry), 2) enable client-side idempotency header so retries are deduped server-side, 3) tweak streaming ACK window in the SDK to 10s by default for your integration.
[03:22] Marcus: are those SDK changes breaking? will it affect our CI? we want minimal churn.
[03:30] Omar: non-breaking — we'll provide a migration guide. the idempotency header is optional and safe. the ACK window default is configurable in the client constructor.
[03:40] Priya: what's the ETA on Redwood providing the patched SDK and the migration notes?
[03:45] Maya: owen — sorry, omar — how fast can you get them?
[03:48] Omar: i can send a build and migration doc within 48 hours, so by friday 2026-05-01.
[03:56] Lena: great. second area i want to dig into is structured output mismatches — sometimes the model returns slightly different keys and our parser throws. is there a way to get a stricter schema enforcement or a confidence score in the response?
[04:14] Omar: yes — two options: 1) function-calling with strict JSON schema enforcement (we can instruct the runtime to validate against your JSON Schema and surface errors instead of raw text), or 2) use our structured-output wrapper which returns a model confidence score and a sanitized JSON object. both approaches are supported on hosted and dedicated.
[04:36] Marcus: our current flow uses function-calling but we had an off-case where the model emitted trailing text outside the JSON. the wrapper sounds promising — does it add latency?
[04:44] Omar: marginally, typically +20–50ms because of the additional validation step. but it prevents post-parse failures which cost you more downstream.
[04:52] Raj: from compliance i'd prefer server-side validation and strict schema enforcement so we avoid PII or malformed outputs being ingested. also need audit logs for schema-violation events.
[05:05] Maya: would Redwood's audit logs include the original model output? we usually redact by default, but we can include hashes and schema-failure flags.
[05:14] Omar: correct — we store metadata and a redacted snapshot; full text can be included in encrypted logs for a limited retention window if you need it for debugging and compliance. that's gated by your contract.
[05:27] Marcus: good to know. next, batching and throughput — some tests show that when we drive higher qps (140–200 rps) we see 2x tail latency spikes. is that expected on hosted?
[05:40] Omar: depends — hosted is multi-tenant, we have autoscaling but tail latency can show up under bursty patterns. two levers: 1) per-tenant reservation (dedicated) for predictable tail, 2) tune batching window to lower latency at the expense of cost. for your pilot throughput, we recommend a small dedicated reserve during business hours.
[06:03] Lena: cost impact? Priya: we have a tight budget for the pilot.
[06:09] Maya: we'll send a cost comparison: small dedicated pool vs hosted with burst buffer. it'll include expected unit cost delta and SLA differences.
[06:18] Omar: also note there's a routing option — prefer low-latency variants of the model for interactive paths and fall back to cheaper quantized variants for background tasks. that saves cost without sacrificing interactivity.
[06:32] Marcus: about the fallback you mentioned — we had an incident where Redwood auto-fell back to a 3B quantized variant and the structured output changed (different tokenization), which broke our post-processor. is there a way to pin the model or ensure schema compatibility between fallbacks?
[06:48] Omar: yes you can pin model families for critical routes. also there's a compatibility matrix we can enforce during rollouts; if the fallback would change output shape we can block that auto-fallback and instead route to a nearby region or degrade gracefully with an error flag.
[07:05] Priya: i'd like that behavior — fail closed with an explicit error instead of silently falling back to an incompatible model.
[07:12] Omar: noted — we'll include that in the pilot config.
[07:17] Raj: quick VPC/KMS question — if we go private or dedicated in our VPC, can Redwood integrate with our HSM-backed KMS for key operations and still support trace uploads to Redwood console? we have strict data residency needs.
[07:34] Omar: yes — in Private mode we can support customer-managed KMS and keep inference logs inside your VPC; optional forwarding of redacted traces to Redwood console is configurable. for HSM there is some onboarding time but it's supported.
[07:49] Lena: ok timeline-wise, when would that be feasible? we can't do full private for the pilot but we might want a staged plan.
[07:56] Maya: pragmatic approach — continue pilot on hosted with the mitigations (SDK upgrade, idempotency header, extended ACK window), validate behavior for two weeks, then if the duplicate invocation rate doesn't drop below 5% consider a short dedicated reserve test for business hours. if that passes, we scope Private/KMS in the next phase.
[08:19] Marcus: what about tracing — we need X-Request-ID correlated across SDK -> Redwood -> function invocation. how do we get those in logs?
[08:28] Omar: you can pass a correlation id header; we'll preserve and surface it in per-request traces. i'll put the header name and example into the migration doc.
[08:36] Priya: ok sounds good. any other blockers?
[08:40] Raj: one more: retention and deletion policies — if we log full outputs for debugging we need support for prompt redaction and deletion on request. does Redwood support on-demand redaction?
[08:51] Omar: yes; we have an API to request deletion of brackets of logs and redaction tools for prompt and output. we'll include that in the security checklist Maya delivers.
[09:00] Maya: wrapping up — let's confirm the immediate timeline: Omar sends SDK build + migration doc by 2026-05-01, Marcus shares lockfiles and sample payloads by 2026-05-01, Maya sends pricing addendum and security checklist by 2026-04-30, Omar to schedule VPC/KMS deep dive with Raj for week of 2026-05-04.
[09:26] Marcus: quick note — we'd like the benchmark to include the streaming ACK window change and the idempotency header to see real effect; i'll provide the harness.
[09:36] Omar: perfect — we'll run hosted vs small dedicated reserve with your harness and publish a short report.
[09:42] Lena: thanks all. one small ask — can you include an example of server-side idempotency header format and how duplicates are deduped in the logs?
[09:51] Omar: yes example and a sample trace will be in the doc.
[09:55] Priya: thanks everyone, this was useful.
[09:59] Maya: thanks for the time. we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
[10:03] End of call.

References mentioned:
- SDK versions: 0.9.2 (customer), 0.9.3 (Redwood patch)
- Pilot success criteria: <5% duplicate invocations, median latency < 350ms for sync paths
- Proposed mitigations: SDK upgrade, idempotency header, extend ACK window, server-side schema validation, optional dedicated reserve

Attachments to be shared after call (not in transcript): migration_guide.pdf (from Redwood), pilot_pricing_addendum.xlsx, security_checklist_aether.pdf, benchmark_plan.csv
